title: COMI-LINGUA: Expert Annotated Large-Scale Dataset for Multitask NLP in Hindi-English Code-Mixing
venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2025
problem_statement: The lack of large-scale, high-quality, human-annotated datasets and standardized benchmarks for Hindi-English (Hinglish) code-mixing across both Devanagari and Roman scripts and diverse core NLP tasks, which limits the training, evaluation, and diagnostic error analysis of multilingual large language models on complex code-mixed text.
domain: Multilingual Natural Language Processing (NLP), Code-Mixing / Code-Switching, Hindi-English (Hinglish) across Roman and Devanagari scripts from social media, news portals, and digital archives.
theoretical_framework: Matrix Language Frame theory (specifically Matrix Language Identification to determine the dominant language dictating syntactic structure) and Code-Mixing Index (CMI) formulation for quantifying code-mixing intensity.
methodology: The authors curate raw Hinglish text from news portals, social media platforms (X, YouTube), political channels, and official archives, filtering sentences by Code-Mixing Index (CMI >= 9), sentence length (>= 5 tokens), profanity, and hate speech. They employ a two-stage annotation pipeline using the COMMENTATOR framework where initial pre-annotations generated by NLP tools and LLMs (Microsoft LID, CodeSwitch, LLaMA 3.3) are manually reviewed and corrected by three bilingual graduate-level experts across five core tasks (LID, MLI, NER, POS tagging, and Machine Translation into Standard English, Romanized Hindi, and Devanagari Hindi), resolving conflicts via majority voting (>= 2/3 agreement). They benchmark traditional tools (Microsoft LID, codeswitch), open-weight LLMs (LLaMA-3.3-70B, LLaMA-3.1-8B, Mistral-7B, Aya-Expanse-8B, Qwen2.5-7B), and closed-weight LLMs (Claude 3.5 Sonnet, GPT-4o, Gemini 1.5 Flash, Command-A-03-2025) under zero-shot and one-shot in-context learning, and perform LoRA parameter-efficient fine-tuning on 7-8B open-weight models.
datasets: COMI-LINGUA (125,615 filtered instances; 376,845 manual expert annotations across LID, MLI, NER, POS tagging, and MT)
Supplementary seed data from prior corpora: PHINC (Srivastava & Singh, 2020), MUTANT (Gupta et al., 2023), Singh et al. (2018c), and YouTube video transcripts (Hugging Face)
News and web sources: NDTV, ABP News, Zee News, News18, TV9, Aaj Tak, X (Twitter), YouTube, INC/BJP/AAP political channels, Mann Ki Baat, Press Information Bureau (PIB)

evaluation.inter_annotator_agreement: Fleiss' Kappa >= 0.817 across all classification tasks (LID: 0.834, MLI: 0.976, NER: 0.852, POS: 0.817; average: 0.863)
evaluation.metrics: Macro Precision, Recall, and Macro F1-score for LID, MLI, NER, and POS; BLEU and chrF++ for Machine Translation evaluated disaggregated across Standard English (Ben, cFen), Romanized Hindi (Brh, cFrh), and Devanagari Hindi (Bdh, cFdh)
evaluation.zero_shot_findings: Closed-weight LLMs dominate zero-shot performance (GPT-4o: LID F1 92.7, MLI F1 98.1, NER F1 60.1, POS F1 70.1; Claude 3.5 Sonnet: LID F1 92.1, MLI F1 90.0, NER F1 56.7, POS F1 69.0), while traditional specialized tools like codeswitch outperform zero-shot LLMs on POS tagging (88.2 F1)
evaluation.one_shot_findings: One-shot prompting consistently boosts performance across LLMs and tasks, especially for structure-sensitive tasks like NER (Claude 3.5 Sonnet NER F1 increases from 56.7 to 85.0) and MT (LLaMA-3.3-70B achieves 62.2 BLEU in English translation)
evaluation.fine_tuning_findings: LoRA fine-tuning of 7-8B open-weight LLMs on COMI-LINGUA yields dramatic gains over prompting (LLaMA-3.1-8B achieves 94.75 F1 in LID, 93.05 F1 in MLI, 95.25 F1 in NER, 86.17 F1 in POS, 56.1 BLEU in English MT, 73.5 BLEU in Devanagari MT; Aya-Expanse-8B achieves 98.77 F1 in MLI, 94.90 F1 in NER, 88.61 F1 in POS)

key_findings: COMI-LINGUA is established as the largest manually annotated Hinglish code-mixed dataset to date, containing 125,615 instances and over 376K expert annotations across five core NLP tasks with high inter-annotator agreement (Fleiss' Kappa >= 0.817).

Closed-weight LLMs (GPT-4o, Claude 3.5 Sonnet) substantially outperform open-weight models in zero-shot settings on most tasks, whereas traditional specialized tools (codeswitch) remain superior in zero-shot POS tagging.
One-shot in-context learning consistently improves performance across models and tasks, particularly in entity disambiguation and structure-sensitive tasks like NER and MT.
Supervised fine-tuning on COMI-LINGUA enables compact 7-8B open-weight models to match or exceed large proprietary models (e.g., reaching up to 95.25 F1 in NER and 98.77 F1 in MLI).

Qualitative error analysis highlights severe LLM failure modes on code-mixed text, including misclassifying Devanagari-script English borrowings, context truncation on long inputs, output repetition/hallucination, generating Python code snippets instead of task predictions, and prompt mimicry.
scope_and_delimitations: Restricted exclusively to Hindi-English (Hinglish) code-mixed text, filtering out monolingual English/Hindi and other languages.
Covers both Devanagari and Roman scripts across formal (news, press releases) and informal (social media) domains in the Indian subcontinent.

Delimited to five core NLP tasks: Token-level Language Identification (LID), Matrix Language Identification (MLI), Named Entity Recognition (NER), Part-Of-Speech (POS) Tagging, and Machine Translation (MT into English, Romanized Hindi, and Devanagari Hindi).
Requires a Code-Mixing Index (CMI) >= 9 and sentence length >= 5 tokens for raw instance retention.

Empirical evaluation is delimited to traditional toolkits (Microsoft LID, codeswitch), 7B-70B open-weight LLMs, and commercial closed-weight LLMs under zero-shot, one-shot, and LoRA fine-tuning paradigms.

limitations.verbatim_excerpt:
While this study offers valuable insights into the annotation and processing of Hinglish code-mixed text, several limitations warrant consideration:

- 1. Language Pair Specificity: The findings derived from Hinglish code-mixed data may not generalize to other language pairs (e.g., Spanish-English), given differences in syntactic structure, sociolinguistic norms, and code-switching behavior.
- 2. Demographic Bias: The use of a relatively small and homogeneous group of annotators may introduce demographic bias, potentially limiting the broader applicability and reliability of the acceptability ratings.
- 3. Resource Constraints: Scaling this work to other code-mixed language pairs remains challenging due to the scarcity of high-quality annotated corpora and the limited availability of models capable of robustly handling diverse code-mixing phenomena.
- 4. Computational Accessibility: While finetuning shows substantial improvements, computational requirements and the need for substantial training data may limit accessibility for resource-constrained settings.
limitations.summary: The authors acknowledge four primary limitations: (1) findings are specific to Hindi-English and may not generalize to other code-mixed language pairs with different syntactic or sociolinguistic dynamics; (2) reliance on a small, homogeneous group of three annotators may introduce demographic bias; (3) scaling the curation to other code-mixed pairs is constrained by scarce corpora and robust models; and (4) high computational requirements for fine-tuning may restrict accessibility in resource-constrained environments.

generalizability_gap: The dataset and empirical findings are restricted exclusively to Hindi-English (Hinglish) code-mixed text within the Indian subcontinent and may not generalize to other code-mixed language pairs, language families, or sociolinguistic environments. In addition, the small, homogeneous pool of three graduate annotators may limit demographic and dialectal representativeness.
methodological_gap: The dataset creation workflow relied on automated pre-annotation tools (Microsoft LID, CodeSwitch, LLaMA 3.3) followed by manual post-editing, which introduces potential pre-annotation bias. Furthermore, LLM evaluation was constrained to zero-shot and fixed one-shot prompts without exploring few-shot scaling or chain-of-thought prompting, and parameter fine-tuning was limited to compact 7-8B models due to compute constraints.
future_work: Scaling dataset curation and annotation frameworks to other under-resourced code-mixed language pairs beyond Hinglish.
Incorporating active learning and iterative refinement pipelines to sustain performance gains and reduce manual annotation overhead.
Expanding annotator demographic diversity to capture wider regional and dialectal language variations.
Developing script-aware and context-sensitive modeling architectures to better handle cross-script borrowed words, mitigate hallucinations, and prevent context truncation in compact LLMs.
